record.original_question: Do there exist abstract polytopes P and Q such that there is at least one amalgamation R with all facets isomorphic to P and all vertex-figures isomorphic to Q, while the polytope P itself has at least two non-isomorphic vertex-figures?

evidence.quote: Problem 15. Are there polytopes P and Q such that hP, Qi is nonempty and P has at least two non-isomorphic vertex-figures?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank $n$ is a partially ordered set $(P,\le)$ with a strictly monotone rank function onto $\{-1,0,1,\dots,n\}$, with a unique minimum element (of rank $-1$) and a unique maximum element (of rank $n$), such that every maximal chain (flag) has exactly $n+2$ elements, $P$ is strongly flag-connected, and the diamond condition holds: whenever $F<G$ with $\operatorname{rank}(G)-\operatorname{rank}(F)=2$, there are exactly two elements $H$ with $F<H<G$. The elements of rank $n-1$ are the facets; for a vertex (element of rank $0$) $v$, the vertex-figure at $v$ is the section $\{F\in P: v\le F\le \hat 1\}$, which is itself an abstract polytope of rank $n-1$.

Given abstract polytopes $P$ and $Q$, an amalgamation of $P$ and $Q$ is an abstract polytope $R$ (of rank one greater than $P$) all of whose facets are isomorphic to $P$ and all of whose vertex-figures are isomorphic to $Q$. Let $\langle P,Q\rangle$ denote the class of all such amalgamations.

Determine whether there exist abstract polytopes $P$ and $Q$ such that:
(i) $\langle P,Q\rangle$ is nonempty, i.e., at least one amalgamation $R$ with facets isomorphic to $P$ and vertex-figures isomorphic to $Q$ exists; and
(ii) the polytope $P$ itself has at least two vertex-figures that are not isomorphic to each other.
